title: EFC — Integrated Hypothesis: Time and Entropy
description: Proposes an Energy-Flow Cosmology (EFC) in which time emerges from energy-flow dynamics modulated by entropy within a Grid-Higgs spacetime. The work links energy flow Ef(S), a variable light speed c(S), and an emergent time relation t(k, S, dEf/dt), and replaces dark matter with halo-mediated entropy regulation. It outlines falsifiable predictions for CMB small-scale anisotropies, gravitational lensing in low-entropy regions, and nHz gravitational-wave propagation effects, while noting the need to calibrate key constants and test relativity compatibility.

energy_flow_vs_entropy.description: Energy flow decreases linearly with entropy S from the initial state (S=0) to maximal dispersion (S=1); E0 is the Planck-scale vacuum energy density scale.

energy_flow_rate.description: Cosmic expansion is driven by the rate of energy-flow change, proportional to volume V and the pressure-to-entropy change ratio, with coupling constant \gamma.

emergent_time.description: Time emerges from the entropy change relative to the energy-flow rate, with k a proportionality constant to be calibrated.

vsl_relation.description: Effective light speed varies with the energy-density state \rho(S) derived from E_f(S); variations are expected only near extreme S.

consciousness_complexity.description: Informational complexity (IIT-inspired \Phi) scales with energy flow and integration capacity I, peaking near S \approx 0.5 (speculative, testable via EEG).

key_results.main_finding: Within the Grid-Higgs framework, time emerges from the entropy-modulated energy flow, with qualitative consistency claimed for a ~0.05% CMB TT excess at l≈2500, enhanced lensing in low-entropy regions, and GR-consistent GW speeds with nHz-scale testable deviations.

sealed_predictions.statement: A ~0.05% excess in the CMB TT power spectrum at multipoles l ≈ 2500 relative to baseline ΛCDM, attributable to entropy-modulated energy flow.
sealed_predictions.falsifiable_by: High-precision CMB measurements (Planck + ACT + SPT + Simons Observatory) showing no such excess within combined systematics and statistical errors.

sealed_predictions.statement: Enhanced gravitational lensing (convergence/shear) in astrophysical regions with low entropy (e.g., cool-core clusters), beyond ΛCDM expectations without invoking non-baryonic dark matter.
sealed_predictions.falsifiable_by: Joint weak/strong-lensing mass reconstructions and X-ray/thermal proxies of entropy showing no positive correlation between lensing strength and low-entropy indicators.

sealed_predictions.statement: Frequency-dependent deviations in nHz gravitational-wave propagation consistent with a small dispersion around ~5 nHz due to c(S)-induced effects.
sealed_predictions.falsifiable_by: PTA datasets (NANOGrav, EPTA, PPTA) consistent with a dispersionless GR background at nHz frequencies to limits excluding the predicted deviation.

sealed_predictions.statement: Strong-lens quasar time delays include residuals at the ~10^{-3} s level after standard modeling, consistent with environment-dependent c(S).
sealed_predictions.falsifiable_by: JWST/HST time-delay cosmography finding residuals below 10^{-4} s with no environment correlation, within calibrated systematics.

kill_criteria: KC1: Combined Planck+ACT+SPT+Simons Observatory analyses rule out any ~0.05% excess at l≈2500 at >3σ relative to ΛCDM, closing the parameter space of Eq. (1)–(2) consistent with the claim.

KC2: Strong/weak lensing maps and rotation curves show no systematic enhancement in low-entropy (cool-core) systems relative to ΛCDM+baryons, or require non-baryonic dark matter with profiles incompatible with halo-regulator substitution.
KC3: PTA constraints demonstrate a dispersionless nHz gravitational-wave background with |vg−c|/c < 10^{-15} across 1–30 nHz, excluding the predicted frequency-dependent effect near ~5 nHz.
KC4: Multi-messenger constraints (e.g., GW170817/GRB170817A-like events and strong-field tests) bound any environment dependence of c to below 10^{-15} with no context variation, falsifying Eq. (4).
KC5: A single global k in the emergent-time relation cannot be jointly calibrated to CMB, lensing, and GW datasets without contradictions (non-overlapping confidence intervals).
KC6: High-resolution CMB/lensing cross-correlations find no measurable coupling between inferred entropy proxies and anisotropy/lensing features, contradicting the Ef(S) driver.

KC7: EEG/information-theoretic studies, after normalization for confounds, find no peak or plateau in Φ-like measures near S ≈ 0.5 across states, undermining the proposed consciousness link (optional but damaging).
